summary: This perspective maps superconducting diodes (SDs) onto circuit quantum electrodynamics (c-QED) architectures, showing how device-level nonreciprocity and Kerr-free nonlinearity address fundamental scalability and control challenges in superconducting quantum processors. SD-integrated platforms promise isothermal classical-quantum hybrid workflows, directional qubit transfer, efficient power management, and quantum-limited amplification without bulky external isolators or circulators.
motivation: Current superconducting quantum hardware faces critical scalability challenges: nonlinear elements are dissipative or require complex multipole circuits, nonreciprocal components (isolators, circulators) are bulky and lossy, and the temperature gradient between room-temperature controls ($T_C \gtrsim$ K) and cryogenic qubits ($T_Q \sim$ mK) dissipates power and introduces noise that shortens coherence times.
method: The authors systematically review superconducting diode mechanisms (intrinsic via symmetry-breaking, extrinsic via vortex dynamics, Josephson-based), analyze their quantum control through broken time-reversal and inversion symmetries, and propose integrating SDs into c-QED for qubits, power delivery, memory, readout, and amplification—highlighted with numerical simulations of transmon chains with twisted NbSe$_2$ Josephson diodes ($\eta \approx 27\%$) and flux-controlled SQUID-resonators enabling nonreciprocal qubit-qubit coupling.
result: Demonstrations include: SD-controlled anharmonicity stabilizing two-level systems in transmon chains with intermediate diode efficiency; nonreciprocal qubit transfer fidelity robust to charge, flux, and dissipative noise; superconducting rectifiers achieving up to 50% efficiency at MHz-GHz frequencies; field-free, Kerr-free third-order nonlinearity ($g_3 \neq 0$, $K = 0$) tunable via gate and flux in SQUID-based elements; path toward topological quantum SDs with dissipationless transport in both directions via quantized chiral edge states.
